1.name: Propeller
1.note: Hub and both blades in one forging. Each blade is a rotating wing whose angle falls from 51° at the root to 15° at the tip, so every station meets the air at a similar α.

2.name: Spinner dome
2.spec: Ø320 × 0.8, cut out round the blades
2.note: Fairs the hub so the air flows smoothly into the cowling inlets. Screwed to the two bulkheads, it turns with the propeller.

3.name: Spinner front bulkhead
3.note: Clamped on the hub's front face under the crush plate; its cone reaches out to hold the spinner dome round and steady part-way along.

4.name: Spinner rear bulkhead
4.note: Sandwiched between the gear support and the hub. The spinner's base sits on its lip and is screwed to it.

5.name: Crush plate
5.note: Spreads the six bolt heads' clamp over the aluminium hub face, so the heads do not dig in and the preload holds.

6.name: Propeller bolt
6.note: Pulls the hub hard against the flange. The friction of that clamp and the drive bushings, not the bolts in shear, carry the engine's torque.

7.name: Washer
7.note: Under each bolt head, on the crush plate: a hard, flat face for the head to turn on while it is torqued.

8.name: Drive bushing
8.note: Pressed into the flange and standing 25 mm proud into counterbores in the hub: the dowels that drive the propeller round. The bolts screw into them.

9.name: Crankshaft flange
9.note: The engine's output: the propeller turns at crankshaft speed with no gearbox. The pilot centres the hub so it runs true.

10.name: Ring gear support
10.spec: Cast plate and skirt, V pulley
10.note: Bolted in the same stack as the propeller. It carries the starter's ring gear and, on its skirt, the pulley that drives the alternator.

11.name: Starter ring gear
11.note: The starter motor's pinion meshes here to crank the engine, and the propeller, over for a start.

12.name: Spinner screw
12.note: Hold the spinner dome to the bulkheads' lips. Each screws into a nutplate, so the spinner comes off from outside.

13.name: Anchor nutplate
13.note: Riveted inside the bulkhead lips: captive, self-locking nuts for the spinner screws.

14.name: Alternator V-belt
14.spec: Single V, in the support's groove
14.note: Taken off the propeller's own rotation: the crankshaft drives the alternator through this belt.

15.name: Safety wire
15.note: Laced through the drilled bolt heads in pairs and twisted, so that a bolt that starts to loosen pulls its neighbour tighter.
